claim: Confidence-Supervised Fine-Tuning (CSFT) — LoRA fine-tuning with cross-entropy loss restricted to a scalar 0-100 <confidence> span, where the label is derived from empirical self-consistency accuracy over K=10 sampled CoT generations — raises GSM8K AUROC from a near-chance 50.57 to 81.25 on LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct.
stance_target: single-model, single-stage SFT distillation of the self-consistency/sampling signal into scalar verbal confidence closes most of the near-chance-to-good-AUROC gap
quoted_support: Our method consistently improves all calibration metrics and accuracy over the pre-trained baseline, not only on LLaMA3.2-3B-Instruct but also on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct.

claim: Pretrained (non-fine-tuned) LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct show near-chance AUROC (50.57 and 49.59 respectively) for verbalized confidence on GSM8K prior to CSFT, mirroring the near-chance verbalized-confidence discrimination reported for code LLMs.
stance_target: verbal confidence elicited by naive prompting is near-chance across domains (math reasoning as well as code), motivating a distillation fix
scope_conditions: GSM8K, pretrained zero-shot baseline before any confidence fine-tuning

claim: CSFT-induced calibration transfers out-of-domain: training only on GSM8K, LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct AUROC on unseen MATH-500 rises from 49.57 to 62.97 (+37% accuracy, -63% ECE) and on unseen ARC-Challenge from 53.89 to 72.58 (-71% ECE).
stance_target: generalizability of a sampling-signal-distilled scalar confidence beyond its training distribution
scope_conditions: zero further fine-tuning on MATH-500/ARC-Challenge; trained only on GSM8K
quoted_support: On MATH-500, LLaMA3.2-3B-Instruct achieves a +37% accuracy gain and 63% ECE reduction... On ARC-Challenge, LLaMA improves accuracy by 6.3% and ECE by 71%

claim: CSFT-trained models spontaneously exhibit emergent self-verification behavior — generating longer, self-checking responses ('let me double check', 'recalculate') for low-confidence queries and shorter, decisive responses for high-confidence queries — despite training only on scalar confidence labels with no explicit self-verification examples or RL reward.
stance_target: distilling a sampling-derived confidence signal into a scalar output can induce beneficial secondary behavior (adaptive reasoning depth) as a side effect, relevant to designing a code-LLM distillation method with similar emergent test-time-scaling properties
scope_conditions: GSM8K and held-out MATH-500/ARC-Challenge, GPT-4.1-judged self-verification rate
quoted_support: Despite being trained only to produce a verbalized confidence score without any self-verifying examples, the model learns to generate longer and self-checking responses for low-confidence queries while providing more concise answers for high-confidence ones.
numbers: lowest-confidence bin output ~5x longer than zero-shot baseline

claim: CSFT is not evaluated on code-generation tasks; all benchmarks are math/commonsense CoT reasoning (GSM8K, MATH-500, ARC-Challenge).
stance_target: domain gap: scalar confidence distillation from self-consistency has not been tested on code LLMs, where unit-test-verified correctness offers a cheaper/more reliable ground-truth signal than exact-match
quoted_support: we fine-tune LLaMA3.2-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, and evaluate accuracy, Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC), and calibration metrics (ECE, Brier Score) on the GSM8K test set as well as on the held-out reasoning benchmarks MATH-500 and ARC-Challenge.

claim: The authors frame prior verbalized-confidence work as reliant on complex RL or classifier-probing procedures with little demonstrated generalization under chain-of-thought reasoning, positioning CSFT's simplicity (masked cross-entropy SFT only) as the key methodological contribution.
stance_target: identifies simplicity/minimal-supervision as a valued property in this literature, relevant to justifying a lightweight single-GPU 7B methodological contribution
quoted_support: most rely on complex procedures such as reinforcement learning or classifier probing. Moreover, they report little evidence of generalization in zero-shot settings or under chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning.
